title: Two Ridges, One Week: Running the Malá Fatra and the Low Tatras

bestPeriod.window: 16 June to the end of September — the high routes are legally shut before that
bestPeriod.avoid: 1 November–15 June (NAPANT and Malá Fatra NP seasonal high-route closure), and wet days on the Rozsutec chains

transport.note: €130–€220 (car hire or bus/train, plus Vrátna and Chopok cable cars)

gatewayAirport: Bratislava (BTS) or Vienna (VIE) then rail to **Žilina** (2 h 30 from Bratislava); Žilina → Terchová by SAD bus, ~50 min. Krakow (KRK) is 3 h by road. Between the ranges: Terchová → Liptovský Mikuláš, ~100 km / 1 h 20 via Žilina and the D1.

hook: The Krivánska Malá Fatra is Slovakia's most concentrated ridge — grass, limestone and chains packed into 20 km — and Veľký Rozsutec at the end of it is a rock horn you climb with your hands. Then you drive ninety minutes east and the Nízke Tatry give you the opposite: a long, rolling, above-treeline crest where Chopok to Ďumbier can be run. Two ranges, two temperaments, one week, and a legal closure you cannot argue with.

snapshot.Best period: 16 June–30 September; best of all in September
snapshot.Start / End: Terchová → Liptovský Mikuláš (linear, ~120 km run, ~7,000 m of vertical)
snapshot.Getting there: Bratislava (BTS) or Vienna (VIE) then rail to **Žilina** (2 h 30 from Bratislava); Žilina → Terchová by SAD bus, ~50 min. Krakow (KRK) is 3 h by road. Between the ranges: Terchová → Liptovský Mikuláš, ~100 km / 1 h 20 via Žilina and the D1.

itinerary.title: Terchová, and a gorge to loosen the legs
itinerary.morning: Bus or drive from Žilina to **Terchová**, birthplace of Juraj Jánošík, the outlaw whose 8 m tin statue stands above the village, and home of the Terchovská muzika string tradition on the UNESCO intangible heritage list.
itinerary.afternoon: The **Jánošíkove diery** from Podžiar: Dolné diery's ladders and catwalks, then the loop through Nové diery and back via Štefanová. Check the weather first — wet rock here is genuinely dangerous, and the one-way system means you cannot simply reverse out.
itinerary.evening: Move up the valley to **Štefanová**, a preserved hamlet of log houses with no through traffic. Bryndzové halušky and a Kofola, then sleep with the Rozsutec silhouette over the roofs.

itinerary.title: The Krivánska ridge, west half
itinerary.morning: Cable car from Vrátna to **Snilovské sedlo (1,524 m)** for a fast start [VERIFY: 2026 Vrátna cable car tariff, operating hours and any maintenance closure], then the short out-and-back to **Veľký Kriváň (1,709 m)** for the whole-range view before turning east.
itinerary.afternoon: The red waymark over **Chleb (1,646 m)**, **Hromové (1,636 m)** and the **Steny** section, where the trail runs along the top of a limestone wall with the Vrátna valley 800 m below on the right. Drop to **Chata pod Chlebom** for water, then run the grass to **Poludňový Grúň**.
itinerary.evening: Descend to **Chata na Grúni** for the terrace and a plate of halušky, then down to Štefanová. Total valley-floor version of this day is close to 2,000 m of vertical if you skip the lift — a legitimate and much better session.

itinerary.title: Stoh, Medziholie and the chains of Veľký Rozsutec
itinerary.morning: Up from Štefanová to **Stoh (1,607 m)**, a steep grass cone with a summit the size of a table. Then the loose descent to **Medziholie (1,185 m)**, the saddle between the two halves of the range.
itinerary.afternoon: **Veľký Rozsutec (1,610 m)** — steel chains and staples on the upper rock, one-way ascent enforced by signs, and a genuinely airy top. Come down north over **Medzirozsutec** and **Malý Rozsutec (1,344 m)** into the Horné diery, which returns you to Štefanová through waterfalls.
itinerary.evening: Pizza and beer at one of the Štefanová chalets, and honest self-assessment: this is the hardest technical day of the week and it tells you whether the Nízke Tatry crest should be run or walked.

itinerary.title: Transfer east, valley legs, and the caves
itinerary.morning: Drive or bus Terchová → Žilina → **Liptovský Mikuláš**, roughly 100 km and 1 h 20 on the D1. Base yourself in **Demänovská Dolina** or in Liptovský Mikuláš itself for supermarkets and physio.
itinerary.afternoon: An easy shakeout in **Demänovská dolina** past **Vyvieranie**, the resurgence where the underground river reappears, then the **Demänovská jaskyňa slobody** or the **Demänovská ľadová jaskyňa** — guided tours only, fixed departure times, and they sell out in August [VERIFY: 2026 Demänovská cave tour times and ticket prices].
itinerary.evening: Liptovský Mikuláš for dinner and the **Múzeum Janka Kráľa** on the main square, then early to bed. Tomorrow is the range's high point.

itinerary.title: Chopok to Ďumbier on the main crest
itinerary.morning: Start at **Trangoška (1,130 m)** on the south side and climb the red waymark to **Chata M. R. Štefánika (1,728 m)**, the classic hut under Ďumbier — coffee, water, and the only shelter on the ridge.
itinerary.afternoon: Up to **Ďumbier (2,043 m)**, the highest point in the Nízke Tatry, with the whole High Tatras chain on the northern horizon. West along the crest over Krúpova hoľa to **Chopok (2,024 m)** — blocky and slow at first, then fast gravel. Descend the south side via Kosodrevina to Trangoška, or take the Jasná lifts down the north side into Demänovská.
itinerary.evening: Recovery in Liptovský Mikuláš — the **Tatralandia** thermal complex is unashamedly a waterpark but the 38 °C outdoor pools do the job [VERIFY: current hours and entry price].

itinerary.title: Bystrá dolina and the long runnable valleys
itinerary.morning: **Bystrá dolina** from Trangoška: forest track and single trail up a quiet valley on the Ďumbier massif's south flank, gaining height gently enough that you can actually run all of it.
itinerary.afternoon: Cross toward **Chopok Juh / Srdiečko** and drop back, or, if legs are good, take the yellow link over to the head of Demänovská and finish down the valley. The alternative base for this day is **Donovaly**, 40 km west, whose forest and meadow network is gentler and better in bad weather.
itinerary.evening: Last big dinner: bryndzové pirohy, kapustnica, and a Demänovka herbal bitter that tastes exactly like the valley it is named after.

itinerary.title: Chopok at dawn, then out
itinerary.morning: First lift up the Jasná side, out to **Chopok (2,024 m)** for sunrise over the Liptov basin, then a fast run down the north-side red-and-blue trails into Demänovská before the cable cars fill.
itinerary.afternoon: Clean kit, return the car, and walk the **Liptovský Mikuláš** old town. If there is time, the open-air museum at **Pribylina** or the Havránok Celtic hillfort above the Liptovská Mara reservoir.
itinerary.evening: Train west to Žilina and Bratislava, or east to Poprad for the High Tatras if you are not finished.

accommodationStrategy.name: A Štefanová chalet
accommodationStrategy.description: Štefanová is inside the national park at the foot of Rozsutec, closed to through traffic, and every route on Days 1–3 starts from the doorstep. No transfers, no parking fees, and you can decide on the weather at 06:00 instead of the night before.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 4–8 weeks ahead for July–August; Štefanová has very few beds [VERIFY: current rates].

accommodationStrategy.name: Chata pod Chlebom
accommodationStrategy.description: sleeping on the ridge means running the Krivánska crest at dawn with no lift queue and no 800 m of morning climbing. Basic bunks, a spring, and a warden who knows the conditions on Rozsutec better than any forecast.
accommodationStrategy.booking: direct with the hut by phone or its own booking form — Slovak huts are not on a central system [VERIFY: current bed rate and season].

accommodationStrategy.name: Chata M. R. Štefánika
accommodationStrategy.description: the only accommodation on the Nízke Tatry main crest, which turns Day 5 from a 1,450 m day into two comfortable halves and puts you on Ďumbier for sunrise. Half-board, shared rooms, no card machine in practice.
accommodationStrategy.booking: direct with the hut, 3–6 weeks ahead for summer weekends [VERIFY: current bed rate and half-board price].

logistics.connectivity: O2, Orange, Telekom and 4ka cover both crests well — the Malá Fatra ridge sees Žilina and the Nízke Tatry crest sees the Liptov basin. Signal drops in the Jánošíkove diery, in Bystrá dolina and in the lower Vrátna forest.
logistics.emergency: **112**, or **18 300** direct to the **Horská záchranná služba (HZS)**, Slovakia's mountain rescue service. Install the HZS app, which transmits your position with the call. **HZS intervention is charged to the person rescued** — travel insurance that explicitly covers mountain rescue and helicopter evacuation in Slovakia is effectively mandatory, and a European Health Insurance Card does **not** cover rescue costs.
logistics.weather: Both crests are fully exposed. Storms build from early afternoon in July and August, and the Malá Fatra ridge in particular funnels wind — 70–90 km/h gusts on Steny are not unusual outside summer. Fog on the Nízke Tatry crest between Chopok and Ďumbier hides the waymarks; carry a compass bearing and a headtorch even on a day run.
logistics.bookingWindows: Huts 3–8 weeks for summer weekends; Štefanová beds 4–8 weeks. Demänovská cave tours 1–2 weeks in August. Insurance before you leave home.
logistics.money: Slovakia uses the **euro**, so no conversion. Cards work in Terchová, Liptovský Mikuláš and the lift stations; **mountain huts are cash-only in practice** — carry €150–€250 in small notes.
logistics.transportRules: A motorway **diaľničná známka** e-vignette is required for the D1 between Žilina and Liptovský Mikuláš — buy online at eznamka.sk, it is plate-linked with no sticker [VERIFY: 2026 e-vignette 10-day and monthly prices]. Vrátna dolina charges for parking in season. SAD buses serve Terchová from Žilina and Demänovská from Liptovský Mikuláš roughly hourly, thinning at weekends.
logistics.permits: No permit, but hard rules. **Trails in the high zones of NAPANT (Národný park Nízke Tatry) and TANAP are closed each year from 1 November to 15 June**, and **Národný park Malá Fatra applies the same seasonal closure to its high routes** — the closure is legally enforced, fines are issued, and HZS will point out that a rescue from a closed trail is both charged and awkward. Beyond that: stay on marked trails (leaving them is an offence in a Slovak national park), no wild camping, no fires, no bivouacking, and no drones. Dogs must be leashed. [VERIFY: 2026 exact closure dates and any route-specific extensions published by NAPANT and NP Malá Fatra.]

other.label: Bears
other.text: Slovakia has a substantial brown bear population and the Nízke Tatry are among the most active areas. Make noise on forest sections, run with a partner at dawn and dusk, never leave food outside a hut, and if you meet one, stop, do not run, and back away while talking.

proTips: **Check the date before anything else.** Nothing on the crests is legal before 16 June. A trip planned for early June is a valley trip, and there is no negotiating this with a warden.

**Sleep at Chata pod Chlebom.** It converts the Krivánska ridge from a lift-dependent day trip into a dawn traverse with the whole crest to yourself, and the sunrise off Rozsutec is the image people come back for.
**Do Rozsutec in the morning, and only in the dry.** The chains face south-east and dry first; by midday the one-way ascent queues behind hikers, and in rain the limestone is unusable.

**Read the rázcestník times as your pacing tool.** Slovak signpost times are conservative hiking times. Once you know your own ratio to them — most fit runners land at 55–65% — you can plan a whole crest day off the signposts without a watch.
**Buy the rescue insurance, and print the policy number.** HZS charges for intervention. A helicopter off Ďumbier is a four-figure bill, and every Slovak hut warden will ask whether you are covered.
**Run the Nízke Tatry from Trangoška, not from the Chopok lift.** The lift version is 9 km of ridge tourism; from the valley it is a real 1,450 m mountain day with the hut in the middle of it.

**Learn the vocabulary that matters:** *chodník* (trail), *sedlo* (saddle), *rázcestník* (signpost junction), *chata* (hut), *uzavretý* (closed) and *pramen'/studnička* (spring). A closure sign in Slovak is the one word you must not misread.

raw.Run 1 — Jánošíkove diery circuit: 11 km, +650 m. From Biely Potok/Podžiar through **Dolné diery**, **Nové diery** and **Horné diery** — a gorge system of ladders, catwalks and chains through waterfalls, on a one-way system. Grade **T3, but not a running route in the true sense**: the ladders are enforced one-way, the rock is wet limestone, and **it should not be attempted in rain or after heavy rain**. Treat it as an active recovery morning, not a session.
raw.Run 2 — The Krivánska ridge: Chleb–Hromo: 18 km, +1,050 m from **Snilovské sedlo** (1,524 m) if you take the cable car, or **+2,000 m** if you start on the Vrátna valley floor at ~750 m and run the whole thing. Red waymark along the crest: **Chleb (1,646 m)**, **Hromové (1,636 m)**, **Steny (1,571 m)**, **Poludňový Grúň (1,460 m)**, with **Veľký Kriváň (1,709 m)**, the range's high point, an easy out-and-back from Snilovské sedlo. Grade **T2–T3**: grass, dwarf pine and rock steps, mostly runnable, exposed in wind.
raw.Run 3 — Stoh, Medziholie and Veľký Rozsu: 15 km, +1,300 m. The ridge's dramatic east end: **Stoh (1,607 m)**, down to **Medziholie (1,185 m)**, then the chained ascent of **Veľký Rozsutec (1,610 m)** — steel chains and staples on steep rock, one-way in the ascent direction. Grade **T4 / secured scrambling**. Descend north over **Medzirozsutec** to Štefanová. **Do not do the Rozsutec chains in the wet.**
raw.Run 4 — The Nízke Tatry crest: Chopok to: 9 km round trip from the Chopok top station, +450 m; 20 km / +1,450 m if run from **Trangoška** (1,130 m). Red waymark: **Chopok (2,024 m)**, Krúpova hoľa, **Ďumbier (2,043 m)**, the range's high point, with **Chata M. R. Štefánika (1,728 m)** tucked below the summit on the south side. Grade **T3** — blocky granite on the summit ridge, fast gravel and grass between.
raw.Run 5 — Bystrá dolina and Demänovská dol: 16–18 km, +700 m. Long forested valley trails with runnable gradients, linking Trangoška, Bystrá and the head of Demänovská. Grade **T1–T2** and the best pure-running surface of the week.
raw.Terrain: Malá Fatra is **grass over Mesozoic limestone and dolomite** — fast in the dry, greasy in the wet, with sharp karst edges through Rozsutec and the diery. The Nízke Tatry crest is **granite and gneiss with gravel and alpine grass**, plus long belts of **kosodrevina** (dwarf mountain pine) that will scratch bare legs to ribbons. Below the treeline both are spruce root and mud.
raw.The Slovak waymarking system (KST): Trails are marked by the **Klub slovenských turistov** with a horizontal colour band between two white bands, painted on rocks and trees at eye level, with a matching directional signpost (*rázcestník*) at every junction carrying times in hours and minutes, not kilometres. **Red = main ridge and long-distance routes** (the Malá Fatra and Nízke Tatry crests are both red). **Blue and green = connecting routes**, **yellow = short links and shortcuts**. Slovak signposted times are hiking times and honest; a fit runner does roughly 55–65% of them.
raw.Water points: In Malá Fatra: the spring at **Chata pod Chlebom (1,423 m)**, water at **Chata na Grúni (~1,100 m)** and **Chata Vrátna**, and the Vrátna valley streams below the ridge. **The Krivánska crest itself is dry** — carry 1.5–2 L. In the Nízke Tatry: **Chata M. R. Štefánika** below Ďumbier is the only reliable high source, plus **Trangoška** and the springs in Bystrá and Demänovská; the Chopok–Ďumbier crest has none. **Vyvieranie**, the karst resurgence in Demänovská dolina, is a sight rather than a refill.
raw.Bail-outs: Malá Fatra: the **Vrátna–Snilovské sedlo cable car** (up or down), **Chata pod Chlebom**, the descent from Poludňový Grúň to **Chata na Grúni** and Vrátna, and Medziholie down to Štefanová. Nízke Tatry: the **Chopok cable cars** on both the Jasná (north) and Srdiečko/Kosodrevina (south) sides, **Chata M. R. Štefánika**, and the walk-off to **Trangoška**. In both ranges the crest is exposed with almost no shelter — the huts are the plan, not the weather.
